note: Controlled theme vocabulary shared by per-document readings (sources/filings/documents/*.json), Discourse items and the Filings tab. The first five keys are the five reform categories named in the June 18, 2026 show cause orders; the rest are cross-cutting issues the post-order record keeps returning to. Validated by tools/validate-documents.mjs.

themes.label: Study process and queue
themes.gloss: How a large load applies for transmission service and is studied, including alternative transmission technologies.

themes.label: Who pays for upgrades
themes.gloss: Cost-shifting protections, cost-recovery agreements, minimum charges and posted cost data.

themes.label: Co-location and on-site generation
themes.gloss: Loads sited with generation, and netting of behind-the-meter generation.

themes.label: Flexible and curtailable service
themes.gloss: New transmission services for loads willing to limit their use of the grid.

themes.label: Generation serving nearby load
themes.gloss: Studying generation that serves an electrically proximate or co-located load.

themes.label: Load visibility and forecasts
themes.gloss: Defining a large load, registries, telemetry and demand forecasts.

themes.label: Capacity and resource adequacy
themes.gloss: Capacity auctions, backstop procurement and bring-your-own-capacity rules.

themes.label: State and federal authority
themes.gloss: Where FERC's transmission authority ends and state retail authority begins.

themes.label: Collateral and exit terms
themes.gloss: Financial security, withdrawal liability and credit requirements for large loads.

themes.label: Schedule and procedure
themes.gloss: Abeyance, extensions, rehearing, interventions and filing deadlines.
